questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle starts from rest at the origin and moves along the $x$-axis. Its acceleration varies with time $t$ as $a = 12t + 6$ (where $a$ is in $\text{m/s}^2$ and $t$ is in seconds). The ratio of its displacement to its velocity at $t = 2\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
Given acceleration $a = 12t + 6$

Velocity $v = \int a dt = \int (12t + 6) dt = 6t^2 + 6t + C_1$

Since the particle starts from rest, $v = 0$ at $t = 0$, which gives $C_1 = 0$.

$v = 6t^2 + 6t$

Displacement $x = \int v dt = \int (6t^2 + 6t) dt = 2t^3 + 3t^2 + C_2$

Since the particle starts from the origin, $x = 0$ at $t = 0$, which gives $C_2 = 0$.

$x = 2t^3 + 3t^2$

At $t = 2\text{ s}$:

$v = 6(2)^2 + 6(2) = 24 + 12 = 36\text{ m/s}$

$x = 2(2)^3 + 3(2)^2 = 16 + 12 = 28\text{ m}$

Ratio of displacement to velocity is $\dfrac{x}{v} = \dfrac{28}{36} = \dfrac{7}{9}$

Answer: $7 : 9$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car can safely negotiate a flat circular turn at a maximum speed of $90\text{ km/h}$ on a dry road. Due to an oil spill, the coefficient of static friction between the tires and the road drops to one-ninth of its original value. Assuming the radius of the turn remains constant, what is the new maximum safe speed for the car?
questions.solution:
The maximum safe speed of a car on a flat circular track is given by $v = \sqrt{\mu_s r g}$, where $\mu_s$ is the coefficient of static friction, $r$ is the radius of the turn, and $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity.

From the formula, the maximum safe speed is directly proportional to the square root of the coefficient of static friction:

$v \propto \sqrt{\mu_s}$

Let the initial maximum speed be $v_1 = 90\text{ km/h}$ and the initial coefficient of friction be $\mu_1$.

The new coefficient of friction is $\mu_2 = \dfrac{1}{9}\mu_1$.

The new maximum safe speed $v_2$ is:

$\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_2}{\mu_1}}$

$\dfrac{v_2}{90} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{9}}$

$v_2 = 90 \times \dfrac{1}{3} = 30\text{ km/h}$

Answer: $30\text{ km/h}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A block of mass $5 \text{ kg}$ rests on a smooth horizontal surface. It is pulled by a light string that makes an angle of $37^{\circ}$ above the horizontal with a constant force of $50 \text{ N}$. Simultaneously, a constant horizontal opposing force of $10 \text{ N}$ acts on the block. The acceleration of the block is
(Take $\sin 37^{\circ} = \dfrac{3}{5}$, $\cos 37^{\circ} = \dfrac{4}{5}$ and $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$)
questions.solution:
The horizontal component of the pulling force is $F_{x} = F \cos 37^{\circ} = 50 \times \dfrac{4}{5} = 40 \text{ N}$.

The vertical component of the pulling force is $F_{y} = F \sin 37^{\circ} = 50 \times \dfrac{3}{5} = 30 \text{ N}$.

The weight of the block is $mg = 5 \times 10 = 50 \text{ N}$. Since $F_{y} \lt mg$, the block remains on the horizontal surface.

The net force acting on the block in the horizontal direction is $F_{\text{net}} = F_{x} - f_{\text{opposing}}$.

Substituting the given values, $F_{\text{net}} = 40 - 10 = 30 \text{ N}$.

Using Newton's second law, the acceleration of the block is $a = \dfrac{F_{\text{net}}}{m} = \dfrac{30}{5} = 6 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Answer: $6 \text{ m s}^{-2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is moving in the $x$-$y$ plane with an initial kinetic energy of $20\text{ J}$. A constant force $\vec{F} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j})\text{ N}$ acts on the particle as it moves from the coordinates $(1\text{ m}, 2\text{ m})$ to $(3\text{ m}, -1\text{ m})$. The kinetic energy of the particle at the final position is:
questions.solution:
Initial position vector $\vec{r}_i = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j}$

Final position vector $\vec{r}_f = 3\hat{i} - \hat{j}$

Displacement vector $\Delta\vec{r} = \vec{r}_f - \vec{r}_i = (3 - 1)\hat{i} + (-1 - 2)\hat{j} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}$

Work done by the constant force $W = \vec{F} \cdot \Delta\vec{r} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) \cdot (2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j})$

$W = (3)(2) + (4)(-3) = 6 - 12 = -6\text{ J}$

Using the work-energy theorem, $W = K_f - K_i$

$-6 = K_f - 20$

$K_f = 14\text{ J}$

Answer: $14\text{ J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A small block is released from rest from a height of $20\text{ m}$ on a frictionless curved track. At the lowest point, it passes through a short rough horizontal patch where it loses $40\%$ of its kinetic energy due to friction. It then continues to move up another frictionless curved track. The maximum vertical height reached by the block on the second track is:
questions.solution:
By the principle of conservation of mechanical energy, the kinetic energy of the block at the lowest point before entering the rough patch is equal to its initial potential energy.

$K_1 = mgh_1$

The block loses $40\%$ of its kinetic energy on the rough horizontal patch. The remaining kinetic energy is:

$K_2 = K_1 - 0.40 K_1 = 0.60 K_1$

$K_2 = 0.60 mgh_1$

As the block moves up the second frictionless track, its kinetic energy is converted into potential energy. At the maximum height $h_2$, the potential energy is equal to $K_2$.

$mgh_2 = 0.60 mgh_1$

$h_2 = 0.60 h_1$

Substituting $h_1 = 20\text{ m}$:

$h_2 = 0.60 \times 20 = 12\text{ m}$

Answer: $12\text{ m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A thin rectangular metallic plate of dimensions $15 \text{ cm} \times 20 \text{ cm}$ is given a total charge of $12 \mu \mathrm{C}$. Assuming uniform charge distribution, the magnitude of surface charge density on the plate is
questions.solution:
Total charge given to the metallic plate, $Q = 12 \mu\mathrm{C} = 12 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{C}$.

Area of one surface of the plate, $A = 15 \text{ cm} \times 20 \text{ cm} = 300 \text{ cm}^2 = 3 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}^2$.

Since it is a thin metallic plate, the charge distributes uniformly over both of its outer surfaces.

Charge on each surface, $q = \dfrac{Q}{2} = 6 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{C}$.

Surface charge density, $\sigma = \dfrac{q}{A} = \dfrac{6 \times 10^{-6}}{3 \times 10^{-2}} = 2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{C} \mathrm{m}^{-2}$.

Answer: $2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{C} \mathrm{m}^{-2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor stores $40 \text{ mJ}$ of electrostatic energy when connected across a $200 \text{ V}$ DC supply. The capacitance of the capacitor is
questions.solution:
The energy stored in a capacitor is given by the formula:

$U = \dfrac{1}{2} C V^2$

Given:
$U = 40 \text{ mJ} = 40 \times 10^{-3} \text{ J}$
$V = 200 \text{ V}$

Substituting the values into the formula:

$40 \times 10^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times C \times (200)^2$

$40 \times 10^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times C \times 40000$

$40 \times 10^{-3} = 20000 \times C$

$C = \dfrac{40 \times 10^{-3}}{20000}$

$C = 2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ F}$

$C = 2 \mu\text{F}$

Answer: $2 \mu\text{F}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor acquires a charge of $40\ \mu\text{C}$ when connected across a $20\ \text{V}$ battery. If the same capacitor is instead connected across a $60\ \text{V}$ battery, its capacitance will be:
questions.solution:
The capacitance of a capacitor is given by the formula $C = \dfrac{Q}{V}$.

Substituting the given values:

$C = \dfrac{40\ \mu\text{C}}{20\ \text{V}} = 2\ \mu\text{F}$

The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor depends only on its physical dimensions (area of the plates and the distance between them) and the dielectric medium between the plates. It is independent of the voltage applied across it or the charge stored in it.

Therefore, when the same capacitor is connected across a $60\ \text{V}$ battery, its capacitance remains unchanged at $2\ \mu\text{F}$.

Answer: $2\ \mu\text{F}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two cylindrical wires, A and B, are made of the same conducting material. The radius of wire A is twice the radius of wire B. If wire A carries a current that is three times the current carried by wire B, what is the ratio of the drift speed of electrons in wire A to that in wire B?
questions.solution:
The drift speed of electrons in a conductor is given by $v_d = \dfrac{I}{neA}$

Since both wires are made of the same material, the free electron density $n$ is the same for both wires. The cross-sectional area is $A = \pi r^2$.

Therefore, the drift speed is proportional to $\dfrac{I}{r^2}$

Given that $r_A = 2r_B$ and $I_A = 3I_B$

The ratio of drift speeds is $\dfrac{v_{dA}}{v_{dB}} = \left(\dfrac{I_A}{I_B}\right) \left(\dfrac{r_B}{r_A}\right)^2$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{v_{dA}}{v_{dB}} = (3) \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{3}{4}$

The ratio of the drift speed of electrons in wire A to that in wire B is $3 : 4$.

Answer: $3 : 4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a laboratory experiment to verify Ohm's law, a student measures the potential difference across a nichrome wire as $V = (90 \pm 1.8)\text{ V}$ and the current passing through it as $I = (3.0 \pm 0.15)\text{ A}$. The calculated resistance of the wire, taking into account the limits of error, is:
questions.solution:
Given $V = 90 \pm 1.8 \text{ V}$ and $I = 3.0 \pm 0.15 \text{ A}$.

From Ohm's law, the resistance is given by $R = \dfrac{V}{I}$.

Substituting the nominal values:

$R = \dfrac{90}{3.0} = 30 \Omega$

The maximum fractional error in resistance is the sum of the fractional errors in voltage and current:

$\dfrac{\Delta R}{R} = \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} + \dfrac{\Delta I}{I}$

$\dfrac{\Delta R}{30} = \dfrac{1.8}{90} + \dfrac{0.15}{3.0}$

$\dfrac{\Delta R}{30} = 0.02 + 0.05 = 0.07$

The absolute error in resistance is:

$\Delta R = 30 \times 0.07 = 2.1 \Omega$

Thus, the calculated resistance with limits of error is $(30 \pm 2.1) \Omega$.

Answer: $(30 \pm 2.1) \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cylindrical metallic wire of initial resistance $5 \Omega$ is drawn so that its length becomes three times its original length. This elongated wire is then folded to form a closed equilateral triangle. What will be the equivalent resistance between any two vertices of this triangle?
questions.solution:
Let the initial length of the wire be $L_0$ and the initial area of cross-section be $A_0$.

The initial resistance is given by $R_0 = \rho \dfrac{L_0}{A_0} = 5 \Omega$.

When the wire is drawn to three times its original length, the new length is $L = 3L_0$. Since the volume of the wire remains constant, $A_0 L_0 = A L$, which gives the new area of cross-section as $A = \dfrac{A_0}{3}$.

The new resistance of the elongated wire is $R = \rho \dfrac{L}{A} = \rho \dfrac{3L_0}{\dfrac{A_0}{3}} = 9 \rho \dfrac{L_0}{A_0} = 9R_0$.

Substituting $R_0 = 5 \Omega$, we get $R = 9 \times 5 = 45 \Omega$.

The wire is then folded to form a closed equilateral triangle. The total resistance of $45 \Omega$ is divided equally among the three sides of the triangle.

The resistance of each side of the triangle is $R_{side} = \dfrac{45}{3} = 15 \Omega$.

To find the equivalent resistance between any two vertices, we observe that one side of the triangle is in parallel with the series combination of the other two sides.

The resistance of the series combination is $15 \Omega + 15 \Omega = 30 \Omega$.

The equivalent resistance $R_{eq}$ between the two vertices is the parallel combination of $15 \Omega$ and $30 \Omega$:

$R_{eq} = \dfrac{15 \times 30}{15 + 30} = \dfrac{450}{45} = 10 \Omega$.

Answer: $10 \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a sample of an unknown material is placed in a non-uniform magnetic field, it is observed to experience a net force driving it from the stronger to the weaker part of the field. Which of the following pairs of values could correctly represent the magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) and relative permeability ($\mu_r$) of this material?
questions.solution:
When a material is placed in a non-uniform magnetic field and experiences a net force driving it from the stronger to the weaker part of the field, it exhibits diamagnetism.

For diamagnetic materials, the magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ is small and negative, i.e., $-1 \lt \chi \lt 0$.

The relative permeability $\mu_r$ is related to magnetic susceptibility by the relation $\mu_r = 1 + \chi$.

Since $\chi$ is small and negative, $\mu_r$ must be slightly less than $1$.

Checking the given options, only $\chi = -0.004$ and $\mu_r = 0.996$ satisfy both conditions ($\chi \lt 0$ and $\mu_r = 1 - 0.004 = 0.996$).

Answer: $\chi = -0.004$, $\mu_r = 0.996$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular coil having magnetic moment $\vec{\mu}$ is placed in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$. If the coil is in a state of unstable equilibrium, what is its magnetic potential energy?
questions.solution:
The magnetic potential energy of a magnetic dipole in a uniform magnetic field is given by $U = -\vec{\mu} \cdot \vec{B} = -\mu B \cos \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the magnetic moment $\vec{\mu}$ and the magnetic field $\vec{B}$.

For the coil to be in equilibrium, the net torque acting on it must be zero. The torque is given by $\vec{\tau} = \vec{\mu} \times \vec{B}$, which implies $\tau = \mu B \sin \theta = 0$. This gives $\theta = 0^{\circ}$ or $\theta = 180^{\circ}$.

In a state of unstable equilibrium, the potential energy is maximum. This occurs when $\theta = 180^{\circ}$.

Substituting $\theta = 180^{\circ}$ in the expression for potential energy:

$U = -\mu B \cos(180^{\circ}) = -\mu B (-1) = +\mu B$

Answer: $+\mu B$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two air-cored solenoids, $P$ and $Q$, are constructed using insulated copper wire. Solenoid $P$ has a total of $N$ turns, a radius of $2r$, and a length $L$. Solenoid $Q$ has a total of $3N$ turns, a radius of $r$, and a length $3L$. The ratio of the self-inductance of solenoid $P$ to that of solenoid $Q$ ($L_P : L_Q$) is:
questions.solution:
The self-inductance of a solenoid is given by $L_{self} = \dfrac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l}$, where $N$ is the total number of turns, $A$ is the cross-sectional area, and $l$ is the length.

For solenoid $P$:
$N_P = N$
$A_P = \pi (2r)^2 = 4\pi r^2$
$l_P = L$
$L_P = \dfrac{\mu_0 N^2 (4\pi r^2)}{L} = \dfrac{4\mu_0 N^2 \pi r^2}{L}$

For solenoid $Q$:
$N_Q = 3N$
$A_Q = \pi r^2$
$l_Q = 3L$
$L_Q = \dfrac{\mu_0 (3N)^2 (\pi r^2)}{3L} = \dfrac{9\mu_0 N^2 \pi r^2}{3L} = \dfrac{3\mu_0 N^2 \pi r^2}{L}$

The ratio of their self-inductances is:
$\dfrac{L_P}{L_Q} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Answer: $4 : 3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the AC circuit shown in the figure, a pure capacitor of capacitance $C$ is connected across an alternating source. If the instantaneous current flowing in the circuit is given by $I = I_0 \cos \omega t$, the instantaneous voltage $V_C$ across the capacitor is:
questions.solution:
For a pure capacitor, the relationship between the instantaneous current $I$ and the charge $q$ is given by:

$I = \dfrac{dq}{dt}$

Since the charge on the capacitor is $q = C V_C$, we have:

$I = C \dfrac{dV_C}{dt}$

Rearranging the equation to solve for $V_C$ gives:

$dV_C = \dfrac{I}{C} dt$

Integrating both sides with respect to time $t$:

$V_C = \int \dfrac{I}{C} dt$

Given that the instantaneous current is $I = I_0 \cos \omega t$, substituting this into the integral yields:

$V_C = \int \dfrac{I_0 \cos \omega t}{C} dt$

$V_C = \dfrac{I_0}{C} \int \cos \omega t dt$

$V_C = \dfrac{I_0}{C} \left( \dfrac{\sin \omega t}{\omega} \right)$

$V_C = \dfrac{I_0}{\omega C} \sin \omega t$

Answer: $\dfrac{I_0}{\omega C} \sin \omega t$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal step-down transformer is connected to a $3300 \text{ V}$ transmission line. It is used to power a $220 \text{ V}$, $66 \text{ W}$ electrical appliance. What is the current drawn by the primary coil of the transformer?
questions.solution:
For an ideal transformer, the input power to the primary coil is equal to the output power from the secondary coil.

$P_p = P_s$

$V_p I_p = P_s$

Substituting the given values:

$3300 \times I_p = 66$

$I_p = \dfrac{66}{3300}$

$I_p = 0.02 \text{ A}$

$I_p = 20 \text{ mA}$

Answer: $20 \text{ mA}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Consider the following electromagnetic radiations:
(I) Microwaves
(II) Ultraviolet rays
(III) Infrared rays
(IV) Gamma rays

Which of the following represents the correct descending order of their wavelengths?
questions.solution:
The electromagnetic spectrum in the order of decreasing wavelength is:

Radio waves $ \gt $ Microwaves $ \gt $ Infrared rays $ \gt $ Visible light $ \gt $ Ultraviolet rays $ \gt $ X-rays $ \gt $ Gamma rays

From the given options, the correct descending order of their wavelengths is:

Microwaves (I) $ \gt $ Infrared rays (III) $ \gt $ Ultraviolet rays (II) $ \gt $ Gamma rays (IV)

Answer: $\text{(I)} \gt \text{(III)} \gt \text{(II)} \gt \text{(IV)}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Sustained interference fringes can be formed by the superposition of which of the following light waves?
A. $E = E_0 \sin(kx - \omega t)$
B. $E = E_0 \sin(2kx - 2\omega t)$
C. $E = E_0 \cos(kx - \omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{4})$
D. $E = E_0 \sin(kx - 3\omega t)$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
For sustained interference fringes, the superposing light waves must be coherent.

Coherent waves must have the same frequency (or angular frequency $\omega$) and a constant phase difference.

From the given equations:
Angular frequency of wave A is $\omega$.
Angular frequency of wave B is $2\omega$.
Angular frequency of wave C is $\omega$.
Angular frequency of wave D is $3\omega$.

Waves A and C have the same angular frequency $\omega$.

Therefore, the superposition of waves A and C will form sustained interference fringes.

Answer: A and C

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the emission spectrum of a hydrogen atom, which of the following transitions corresponds to the longest wavelength in the Paschen series?
questions.solution:
For the Paschen series in the hydrogen emission spectrum, the electron transitions from a higher energy level $n_2$ to the lower energy level $n_1 = 3$.

The wavelength $\lambda$ of the emitted photon is given by the Rydberg formula:

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R_H \left( \dfrac{1}{3^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right)$ where $n_2 = 4, 5, 6, \dots$

The longest wavelength corresponds to the minimum energy difference between the two levels. This occurs when the electron transitions from the nearest higher energy level.

Therefore, for the minimum energy and longest wavelength, $n_2 = 4$.

The required transition is $n = 4 \rightarrow n = 3$.

Answer: $n = 4 \rightarrow n = 3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The energy levels of a hypothetical atom are shown in the given figure. Let $\lambda_X$, $\lambda_Y$, and $\lambda_Z$ be the wavelengths of the photons emitted during the transitions $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ respectively. Which of the following mathematical relations is correct?
questions.solution:
The energy of a photon emitted during a transition is given by $\Delta E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.

For transition X (from $-E$ to $-3E$):
$\Delta E_X = -E - (-3E) = 2E$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_X} = 2E \Rightarrow \lambda_X = \dfrac{hc}{2E}$

For transition Y (from $-3E$ to $-7E$):
$\Delta E_Y = -3E - (-7E) = 4E$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_Y} = 4E \Rightarrow \lambda_Y = \dfrac{hc}{4E}$

For transition Z (from $-E$ to $-7E$):
$\Delta E_Z = -E - (-7E) = 6E$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_Z} = 6E \Rightarrow \lambda_Z = \dfrac{hc}{6E}$

Comparing $\lambda_X$ and $\lambda_Y$:
$\dfrac{\lambda_X}{\lambda_Y} = \dfrac{\dfrac{hc}{2E}}{\dfrac{hc}{4E}} = \dfrac{4E}{2E} = 2$
$\Rightarrow \lambda_X = 2\lambda_Y$

Answer: $\lambda_X = 2\lambda_Y$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a nuclear fission reactor, control rods made of materials such as cadmium or boron are used primarily to:
options: slow down the fast-moving neutrons produced during fission
absorb excess neutrons to regulate the power level of the reactor
transfer heat from the reactor core to the steam generator
provide the initial fast neutrons required to start the chain reaction
questions.solution:
In a nuclear fission reactor, control rods are made of neutron-absorbing materials such as cadmium or boron.

Their primary function is to absorb excess neutrons produced during the fission process. By inserting or withdrawing these rods from the reactor core, the number of available neutrons is controlled, which in turn regulates the rate of the chain reaction and the power level of the reactor.

Slowing down fast-moving neutrons is the function of a moderator, while transferring heat is the function of a coolant.

Answer: absorb excess neutrons to regulate the power level of the reactor

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The figure below shows the $V-I$ characteristics of a semiconductor device under different levels of incident light intensity ($E_1, E_2, E_3$).

Based on the given graph, identify the device and its standard operating condition.
options: Light Emitting Diode operated in forward bias
Solar cell operated with no external bias
Zener diode operated in the reverse breakdown region
questions.solution:
Based on the given $V-I$ characteristics graph:

1. The curves are plotted in the third quadrant, which means the device is operating under reverse bias (negative voltage and negative current).

2. The magnitude of the reverse current is in microamperes ($\mu$A) and it remains almost constant over a range of reverse voltages. This is known as the reverse saturation current.

3. The reverse saturation current increases as the intensity of incident light increases ($E_3 \gt E_2 \gt E_1$).

This behavior is characteristic of a photodiode. A photodiode is a semiconductor device that converts light into an electrical current. It is specifically designed to operate in reverse bias. When light falls on the photodiode, it generates electron-hole pairs, which increases the reverse current. This current is directly proportional to the intensity of the incident light.

Therefore, the device is a photodiode operated in reverse bias.

Answer: Photodiode operated in reverse bias

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student uses an error-free screw gauge to measure the thickness of a uniform glass plate. The pitch of the screw gauge is $0.5\text{ mm}$ and there are $50$ divisions on its circular scale. During the measurement, the linear scale reads $2.5\text{ mm}$ and the $34^{\text{th}}$ division of the circular scale aligns with the reference line. The thickness of the glass plate is:
questions.solution:
Least count of the screw gauge is given by:

$\text{LC} = \dfrac{\text{Pitch}}{\text{Number of divisions on circular scale}}$

$\text{LC} = \dfrac{0.5\text{ mm}}{50} = 0.01\text{ mm}$

The thickness of the glass plate is calculated as:

$\text{Thickness} = \text{Linear scale reading} + (\text{Circular scale reading} \times \text{LC})$

$\text{Thickness} = 2.5\text{ mm} + (34 \times 0.01\text{ mm})$

$\text{Thickness} = 2.5\text{ mm} + 0.34\text{ mm} = 2.84\text{ mm}$

Converting to centimeters:

$2.84\text{ mm} = 0.284\text{ cm}$

Answer: $0.284\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A deuteron and an alpha particle are accelerated from rest through potential differences $V_1$ and $V_2$ respectively. If the de-Broglie wavelength associated with both particles is equal, then the ratio $\dfrac{V_1}{V_2}$ is:
questions.solution:
The de-Broglie wavelength of a particle accelerated through a potential difference $V$ is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$, where $m$ is the mass and $q$ is the charge of the particle.

Let the mass of a proton be $m$ and its charge be $e$.

For a deuteron:
Mass $m_1 = 2m$
Charge $q_1 = e$
Wavelength $\lambda_1 = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2(2m)(e)V_1}} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{4meV_1}}$

For an alpha particle:
Mass $m_2 = 4m$
Charge $q_2 = 2e$
Wavelength $\lambda_2 = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2(4m)(2e)V_2}} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{16meV_2}}$

Given that the de-Broglie wavelengths are equal ($\lambda_1 = \lambda_2$):

$\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{4meV_1}} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{16meV_2}}$

Squaring both sides, we get:

$4meV_1 = 16meV_2$

$\dfrac{V_1}{V_2} = \dfrac{16}{4} = \dfrac{4}{1}$

The ratio $\dfrac{V_1}{V_2}$ is $4:1$.

Answer: $4:1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The power $P$ delivered by a machine varies with distance $x$ and time $t$ according to the equation $P = \dfrac{\alpha \sqrt{x}}{\beta + t^2}$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are dimensional constants. The dimensional formula for the quantity $\dfrac{\alpha^2}{\beta}$ is:
questions.solution:
From the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, the quantity $\beta$ must have the same dimensions as $t^2$.

$[\beta] = [\mathrm{T}^2]$

The dimensional formula for power $P$ is $[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^2 \mathrm{T}^{-3}]$ and for distance $x$ is $[\mathrm{L}]$.

Using the given equation $P = \dfrac{\alpha \sqrt{x}}{\beta + t^2}$, the dimensions of $\alpha$ are:

$[\alpha] = \dfrac{[P][\beta + t^2]}{[\sqrt{x}]}$

$[\alpha] = \dfrac{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^2 \mathrm{T}^{-3}][\mathrm{T}^2]}{[\mathrm{L}^{1/2}]} = [\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^{3/2} \mathrm{T}^{-1}]$

The dimensional formula for $\dfrac{\alpha^2}{\beta}$ is:

$\left[\dfrac{\alpha^2}{\beta}\right] = \dfrac{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^{3/2} \mathrm{T}^{-1}]^2}{[\mathrm{T}^2]}$

$\left[\dfrac{\alpha^2}{\beta}\right] = \dfrac{[\mathrm{M}^2 \mathrm{L}^3 \mathrm{T}^{-2}]}{[\mathrm{T}^2]} = [\mathrm{M}^2 \mathrm{L}^3 \mathrm{T}^{-4}]$

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{M}^2 \mathrm{L}^3 \mathrm{T}^{-4}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An astronaut of mass $80\text{ kg}$ is transferred from a space station $P$ to another space station $Q$. As shown in the figure, $P$ and $Q$ are at heights $R$ and $3R$ respectively from the surface of a planet of radius $R$. If the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the planet is $10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, what is the decrease in the gravitational force exerted by the planet on the astronaut when moving from $P$ to $Q$?
questions.solution:
The gravitational force exerted by a planet of mass $M$ and radius $R$ on an object of mass $m$ at a distance $r$ from its center is given by $F = \dfrac{GMm}{r^2}$.

The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the planet is $g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}$, which gives $GM = gR^2$.

The distance of space station $P$ from the center of the planet is $r_P = R + R = 2R$.

The gravitational force on the astronaut at $P$ is:
$F_P = \dfrac{GMm}{(2R)^2} = \dfrac{gR^2m}{4R^2} = \dfrac{mg}{4}$

The distance of space station $Q$ from the center of the planet is $r_Q = R + 3R = 4R$.

The gravitational force on the astronaut at $Q$ is:
$F_Q = \dfrac{GMm}{(4R)^2} = \dfrac{gR^2m}{16R^2} = \dfrac{mg}{16}$

The decrease in gravitational force when moving from $P$ to $Q$ is:
$\Delta F = F_P - F_Q = \dfrac{mg}{4} - \dfrac{mg}{16} = \dfrac{3mg}{16}$

Substituting the given values $m = 80\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$\Delta F = \dfrac{3 \times 80 \times 10}{16} = 150\text{ N}$

Answer: $150\text{ N}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider two ideal gases $X$ and $Y$ at a given temperature. Gas $X$ is a rigid diatomic gas. Gas $Y$ is a non-linear polyatomic gas having two active vibrational modes. If $\gamma_X$ and $\gamma_Y$ represent the ratio of specific heats ($C_p/C_v$) for gas $X$ and gas $Y$ respectively, the ratio $\dfrac{\gamma_X}{\gamma_Y}$ is:
questions.solution:
For gas $X$ (rigid diatomic gas):

Degrees of freedom, $f_X = 3$ (translational) $+ 2$ (rotational) $= 5$

$\gamma_X = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f_X} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{7}{5}$

For gas $Y$ (non-linear polyatomic gas with two active vibrational modes):

Each vibrational mode contributes $2$ degrees of freedom (one for kinetic energy and one for potential energy).

Degrees of freedom, $f_Y = 3$ (translational) $+ 3$ (rotational) $+ 2 \times 2$ (vibrational) $= 10$

$\gamma_Y = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f_Y} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{10} = \dfrac{6}{5}$

Ratio $\dfrac{\gamma_X}{\gamma_Y} = \dfrac{7/5}{6/5} = \dfrac{7}{6}$

Answer: $\dfrac{7}{6}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body oscillates with simple harmonic motion of amplitude $A$. What fraction of its total mechanical energy is kinetic energy when its displacement from the mean position is $\dfrac{A}{3}$?
questions.solution:
Total mechanical energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is $E = \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 A^2$

Kinetic energy at a displacement $x$ is $K = \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 (A^2 - x^2)$

The fraction of kinetic energy to total energy is $\dfrac{K}{E} = \dfrac{A^2 - x^2}{A^2} = 1 - \left(\dfrac{x}{A}\right)^2$

Substituting $x = \dfrac{A}{3}$:

$\dfrac{K}{E} = 1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 = 1 - \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{8}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{8}{9}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A progressive wave travelling in a medium is represented by the equation $y = A \sin(\beta t - \alpha x)$, where $y$, $x$, and $t$ are in SI units. The wavelength of the wave is given by:
questions.solution:
The given equation of the progressive wave is $y = A \sin(\beta t - \alpha x)$.

Comparing this with the standard equation of a progressive wave $y = A \sin(\omega t - k x)$, we get the angular frequency $\omega = \beta$ and the wave number $k = \alpha$.

The wave number $k$ is related to the wavelength $\lambda$ by the relation $k = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}$.

Substituting $k = \alpha$, we get $\alpha = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}$.

Therefore, the wavelength is $\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi}{\alpha}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2\pi}{\alpha}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electric potential of $3 \times 10^4 \text{ V}$ is produced at a distance of $60 \text{ cm}$ from an isolated point charge in air. The magnitude of the point charge is $\left[\text{Take } \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9 \text{ N m}^2 \text{ C}^{-2}\right]$ :
questions.solution:
The electric potential $V$ due to a point charge $q$ at a distance $r$ is given by

$V = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q}{r}$

Substituting the given values:

$3 \times 10^4 = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times q}{0.6}$

$q = \dfrac{3 \times 10^4 \times 0.6}{9 \times 10^9}$

$q = \dfrac{1.8 \times 10^4}{9 \times 10^9}$

$q = 0.2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ C}$

$q = 2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ C}$

Answer: $2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider the circuit shown in the given figure. What will be the charge on the $5\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor in the steady state?
questions.solution:
In the steady state, the capacitor acts as an open circuit. Thus, no current flows through the middle branch containing the $5\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor and the $4\ \Omega$ resistor.

The steady current $I$ flows only through the $2\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$ resistors.

The equivalent resistance of the circuit is:
$R_{\text{eq}} = 2 + 3 = 5\ \Omega$

The current in the circuit is:
$I = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2\text{ A}$

The potential difference across the $3\ \Omega$ resistor is:
$V = I \times 3 = 2 \times 3 = 6\text{ V}$

Since the capacitor branch is in parallel with the $3\ \Omega$ resistor, the potential difference across the capacitor branch is also $6\text{ V}$. As there is no current in this branch, the voltage drop across the $4\ \Omega$ resistor is zero.

Therefore, the potential difference across the capacitor is $V_C = 6\text{ V}$.

The charge on the capacitor is:
$Q = C V_C = 5\ \mu\text{F} \times 6\text{ V} = 30\ \mu\text{C}$

Answer: $30\ \mu\text{C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two different configurations of $n$ identical cells (each having electromotive force $E$ and internal resistance $r$) are shown in the figures. In Figure (a), the cells are connected in series across an external resistor of resistance $R$. In Figure (b), the same cells are connected in parallel across an identical resistor $R$. If the current measured by the ideal ammeter is found to be the same in both the configurations, which of the following conditions is correct? (Assume $n \gt 1$)
questions.solution:
For the series configuration in Figure (a), the equivalent electromotive force (emf) of $n$ cells is $nE$ and the equivalent internal resistance is $nr$.
The current $I_s$ through the circuit is given by:
$I_s = \dfrac{nE}{R + nr}$

For the parallel configuration in Figure (b), the equivalent emf of $n$ identical cells is $E$ and the equivalent internal resistance is $\dfrac{r}{n}$.
The current $I_p$ through the circuit is given by:
$I_p = \dfrac{E}{R + \dfrac{r}{n}} = \dfrac{nE}{nR + r}$

Given that the current is the same in both configurations, we equate $I_s$ and $I_p$:
$\dfrac{nE}{R + nr} = \dfrac{nE}{nR + r}$

Since $nE \neq 0$, we can equate the denominators:
$R + nr = nR + r$

Rearranging the terms, we get:
$nr - r = nR - R$
$r(n - 1) = R(n - 1)$

Since $n \gt 1$, we have $n - 1 \neq 0$. Dividing both sides by $(n - 1)$ yields:
$R = r$

Answer: $R = r$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A small rectangular bar magnet is suspended horizontally in a uniform magnetic field of $50 \mu T$, as shown in the figure. The moment of inertia of the magnet about its axis of suspension is $\dfrac{2 \times 10^{-5}}{\pi^2} \text{ kg m}^2$. If the magnet takes $40 \text{ s}$ to complete 10 small angular oscillations, what is the magnetic moment of the magnet?
questions.solution:
The time period of one oscillation is $T = \dfrac{40}{10} = 4 \text{ s}$.

The formula for the time period of a magnetic dipole oscillating in a uniform magnetic field is:

$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{MB}}$

Squaring both sides and rearranging for the magnetic moment $M$ gives:

$M = \dfrac{4\pi^2 I}{T^2 B}$

Substituting the given values $I = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-5}}{\pi^2} \text{ kg m}^2$, $B = 50 \times 10^{-6} \text{ T}$, and $T = 4 \text{ s}$:

$M = \dfrac{4\pi^2 \times \left(\dfrac{2 \times 10^{-5}}{\pi^2}\right)}{4^2 \times 50 \times 10^{-6}}$

$M = \dfrac{8 \times 10^{-5}}{16 \times 50 \times 10^{-6}}$

$M = \dfrac{8 \times 10^{-5}}{800 \times 10^{-6}}$

$M = \dfrac{10^{-5}}{10^{-4}} = 0.1 \text{ A m}^2$

Answer: $0.1 \text{ A m}^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform straight bar magnet has a magnetic dipole moment $\mu$. It is carefully bent at its exact center to form a V-shape, such that the angle between the two halves is $120^{\circ}$. The new magnetic dipole moment of the system will be:
questions.solution:
Let the initial length of the bar magnet be $2l$ and its pole strength be $m$.

The initial magnetic dipole moment is given by $\mu = m(2l)$.

When the magnet is bent at its exact center, it forms two arms of equal length $l$. The angle between these two arms is given as $120^{\circ}$.

The new distance $d$ between the North and South poles can be calculated using the cosine rule in the triangle formed by the two arms:

$d = \sqrt{l^2 + l^2 - 2(l)(l)\cos(120^{\circ})}$

Substituting $\cos(120^{\circ}) = -\dfrac{1}{2}$:

$d = \sqrt{2l^2 - 2l^2\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \sqrt{2l^2 + l^2} = \sqrt{3}l$

The new magnetic dipole moment $\mu'$ is the product of the pole strength and the new distance between the poles:

$\mu' = m(\sqrt{3}l) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(m \times 2l)$

Substituting the initial magnetic moment $\mu = 2ml$:

$\mu' = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\mu$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\mu$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A coil having an inductance of $0.16\text{ H}$ and a resistance of $12\ \Omega$ is connected to an alternating voltage source given by $V = 200\sqrt{2} \sin(100 t)$, where $V$ is in volts and $t$ is in seconds. The peak current in the circuit and the average power dissipated by the coil are respectively:
questions.solution:
The given alternating voltage is $V = 200\sqrt{2} \sin(100 t)$.

Comparing this with the standard equation $V = V_0 \sin(\omega t)$, we get:
Peak voltage, $V_0 = 200\sqrt{2}\text{ V}$
Angular frequency, $\omega = 100\text{ rad/s}$

The inductive reactance $X_L$ is given by:
$X_L = \omega L = 100 \times 0.16 = 16\ \Omega$

The impedance $Z$ of the coil is:
$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2} = \sqrt{12^2 + 16^2} = \sqrt{144 + 256} = \sqrt{400} = 20\ \Omega$

The peak current $I_0$ in the circuit is:
$I_0 = \dfrac{V_0}{Z} = \dfrac{200\sqrt{2}}{20} = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ A}$

The RMS current $I_{rms}$ is:
$I_{rms} = \dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 10\text{ A}$

The average power dissipated by the coil is:
$P_{avg} = I_{rms}^2 R = (10)^2 \times 12 = 100 \times 12 = 1200\text{ W}$

Answer: $10\sqrt{2}\text{ A}$ and $1200\text{ W}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An unpolarized light beam of initial intensity $I_0$ travels along an optical axis and passes through three polarizing filters $P_1$, $P_2$, and $P_3$ arranged in series, as shown in the figure. The transmission axis of $P_1$ is vertical, while the transmission axis of $P_3$ is horizontal (crossed with respect to $P_1$). The transmission axis of the middle filter $P_2$ is oriented at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with respect to the vertical. What is the intensity of the light emerging from $P_3$?
questions.solution:
When unpolarized light of intensity $I_0$ passes through the first polarizer $P_1$, the intensity of the transmitted light becomes half:

$I_1 = \dfrac{I_0}{2}$

This light is vertically polarized. It then passes through the second polarizer $P_2$, whose transmission axis is at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with respect to the vertical. According to Malus's law, the intensity of light transmitted through $P_2$ is:

$I_2 = I_1 \cos^2(60^{\circ}) = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{I_0}{8}$

The light emerging from $P_2$ is polarized at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ to the vertical. The third polarizer $P_3$ has a horizontal transmission axis, which is at $90^{\circ}$ to the vertical. The angle between the polarization direction of the light incident on $P_3$ and its transmission axis is:

$\theta = 90^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 30^{\circ}$

Applying Malus's law again for $P_3$, the final transmitted intensity $I'$ is:

$I' = I_2 \cos^2(30^{\circ}) = \dfrac{I_0}{8} \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{I_0}{8} \times \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{3I_0}{32}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3I_0}{32}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the circuit shown below, $D_1$ and $D_2$ are silicon diodes. Assuming the knee voltage (barrier potential) of a silicon diode to be $0.7\text{ V}$, what is the current supplied by the battery?
questions.solution:
The positive terminal of the battery is connected to the p-side of diode $D_1$ and the n-side of diode $D_2$.

Therefore, $D_1$ is forward-biased and $D_2$ is reverse-biased.

The branch containing $D_2$ acts as an open circuit, so no current flows through $R_3$.

The active circuit is a series loop with the battery, $R_1$, $D_1$, and $R_2$.

The net voltage driving the current is the battery voltage minus the barrier potential of the forward-biased diode $D_1$.

$V_{net} = 3.7 - 0.7 = 3.0$ V

The equivalent resistance of the active circuit is the sum of the series resistors $R_1$ and $R_2$.

$R_{eq} = R_1 + R_2 = 5 + 5 = 10\ \Omega$

The current supplied by the battery is calculated using Ohm's law.

$I = \dfrac{V_{net}}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{3.0}{10} = 0.30$ A

Answer: $0.30\text{ A}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following gas samples contains the same number of molecules as $3.4\text{ g}$ of ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_3$)?
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\mathrm{NH}_3 = 14 + 3 = 17\text{ g/mol}$

Number of moles of $\mathrm{NH}_3 = \dfrac{3.4}{17} = 0.2\text{ mol}$

Number of molecules is directly proportional to the number of moles. We check the number of moles for each option:

For $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}$, molar mass $= 34\text{ g/mol}$. Moles $= \dfrac{3.4}{34} = 0.1\text{ mol}$

For $\mathrm{O}_2$, molar mass $= 32\text{ g/mol}$. Moles $= \dfrac{8.0}{32} = 0.25\text{ mol}$

For $\mathrm{SO}_2$, molar mass $= 64\text{ g/mol}$. Moles $= \dfrac{12.8}{64} = 0.2\text{ mol}$

For $\mathrm{CO}_2$, molar mass $= 44\text{ g/mol}$. Moles $= \dfrac{4.4}{44} = 0.1\text{ mol}$

Since $12.8\text{ g}$ of $\mathrm{SO}_2$ has $0.2\text{ mol}$, it contains the same number of molecules as $3.4\text{ g}$ of $\mathrm{NH}_3$.

Answer: $12.8\text{ g}$ of $\mathrm{SO}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The atomic radii of the elements $\mathrm{Na}$, $\mathrm{Mg}$, $\mathrm{Al}$, and $\mathrm{Si}$ are given in a random order as $118\text{ pm}$, $143\text{ pm}$, $160\text{ pm}$, and $186\text{ pm}$. Based on the periodic trend, which of the following represents the correct atomic radius of $\mathrm{Al}$?
questions.solution:
The given elements $\mathrm{Na}$, $\mathrm{Mg}$, $\mathrm{Al}$, and $\mathrm{Si}$ belong to the third period of the periodic table.

As we move from left to right across a period, the effective nuclear charge increases, which pulls the valence electrons closer to the nucleus. Consequently, the atomic radius decreases.

The order of atomic radii for these elements is $\mathrm{Na} \gt \mathrm{Mg} \gt \mathrm{Al} \gt \mathrm{Si}$.

Arranging the given values in decreasing order, we get $186\text{ pm} \gt 160\text{ pm} \gt 143\text{ pm} \gt 118\text{ pm}$.

Matching the elements with their corresponding radii:
$\mathrm{Na} = 186\text{ pm}$
$\mathrm{Mg} = 160\text{ pm}$
$\mathrm{Al} = 143\text{ pm}$
$\mathrm{Si} = 118\text{ pm}$

The atomic radius of $\mathrm{Al}$ is $143\text{ pm}$.

Answer: $143\text{ pm}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below is an outline of the modern periodic table where four elements are marked as P, Q, R, and S.

Match List I (the marked elements) with List II (their characteristic properties) based on their positions in the periodic groups.

List IList II
AElement PIHighest negative electron gain enthalpy
BElement QIIMost electronegative element
CElement RIIILowest ionization enthalpy
DElement SIVHighest ionization enthalpy

Identify the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Based on the given outline of the modern periodic table, the elements are identified as follows:

Element P is in Group 1 and Period 6, which corresponds to Cesium (Cs). Cesium has the largest atomic size among stable elements and consequently the lowest ionization enthalpy. Thus, A matches with III.

Element Q is in Group 17 and Period 2, which corresponds to Fluorine (F). Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table. Thus, B matches with II.

Element R is in Group 17 and Period 3, which corresponds to Chlorine (Cl). Chlorine has the highest negative electron gain enthalpy due to its relatively smaller size and higher effective nuclear charge compared to other halogens, but larger size than fluorine which reduces interelectronic repulsions. Thus, C matches with I.

Element S is in Group 18 and Period 1, which corresponds to Helium (He). Helium has a completely filled $1s^2$ shell and the smallest atomic size among noble gases, giving it the highest ionization enthalpy of all elements. Thus, D matches with IV.

The correct matching is A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

Answer: A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider a chemical reaction where the total enthalpy of the products is greater than the total enthalpy of the reactants. Which of the following statements are correct for this process?
(A) The reaction is exothermic in nature.
(B) The enthalpy change ($\Delta_r H$) is positive.
(C) Heat is absorbed by the system at constant pressure ($q_p \gt 0$).
(D) The enthalpy change ($\Delta_r H$) is negative.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Given that the total enthalpy of the products is greater than the total enthalpy of the reactants, $H_P \gt H_R$.

The enthalpy change for the reaction is given by $\Delta_r H = H_P - H_R$.

Since $H_P \gt H_R$, it follows that $\Delta_r H \gt 0$. Thus, the enthalpy change is positive, making statement (B) correct and statement (D) incorrect.

A positive enthalpy change indicates that the reaction is endothermic, meaning heat is absorbed by the system. Therefore, statement (A) is incorrect.

At constant pressure, the heat exchanged is equal to the enthalpy change, $q_p = \Delta_r H$. Since $\Delta_r H \gt 0$, we have $q_p \gt 0$, which means heat is absorbed by the system. Thus, statement (C) is correct.

Therefore, only statements (B) and (C) are correct.

Answer: (B) and (C) only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following two equilibrium reactions at a constant temperature:

(i) $CO(g) + 2H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons CH_3OH(g)$ ; Equilibrium constant $= K_1$
(ii) $3CH_3OH(g) \rightleftharpoons 3CO(g) + 6H_2(g)$ ; Equilibrium constant $= K_2$

Which of the following correctly expresses the relationship between $K_1$ and $K_2$?
questions.solution:
For the first reaction:
$CO(g) + 2H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons CH_3OH(g)$
The equilibrium constant is given by:
$K_1 = \dfrac{[CH_3OH]}{[CO][H_2]^2}$

For the second reaction:
$3CH_3OH(g) \rightleftharpoons 3CO(g) + 6H_2(g)$
The equilibrium constant is given by:
$K_2 = \dfrac{[CO]^3[H_2]^6}{[CH_3OH]^3}$

Rearranging the expression for $K_2$ in terms of $K_1$:
$K_2 = \left( \dfrac{[CO][H_2]^2}{[CH_3OH]} \right)^3$

$K_2 = \left( \dfrac{1}{K_1} \right)^3 = \dfrac{1}{K_1^3}$

Answer: $K_2 = \dfrac{1}{K_1^3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The dissociation of phosphorus pentachloride is an endothermic process:
$\mathrm{PCl}_5(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{g}), \Delta \mathrm{H} \gt 0$
According to Le Chatelier's principle, which of the following conditions will favor the maximum yield of products?
options: High pressure, low temperature, and addition of $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ gas
Low pressure, high temperature, and continuous removal of $\mathrm{PCl}_3$
High pressure, high temperature, and use of a suitable catalyst
Low pressure, low temperature, and increasing the concentration of $\mathrm{Cl}_2$
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $\mathrm{PCl}_5(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{g})$ with $\Delta \mathrm{H} \gt 0$.

According to Le Chatelier's principle:

Since the reaction is endothermic ($\Delta \mathrm{H} \gt 0$), an increase in temperature will shift the equilibrium in the forward direction to absorb the added heat. Thus, high temperature favors the formation of products.

The number of gaseous moles increases from $1$ on the reactant side to $2$ on the product side. A decrease in pressure shifts the equilibrium in the direction of a greater number of gaseous moles. Thus, low pressure favors the forward reaction.

Continuous removal of a product (such as $\mathrm{PCl}_3$) decreases its concentration, which shifts the equilibrium in the forward direction to produce more products.

Therefore, low pressure, high temperature, and continuous removal of $\mathrm{PCl}_3$ will favor the maximum yield of products.

Answer: Low pressure, high temperature, and continuous removal of $\mathrm{PCl}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During the titration of ammonium hydroxide (taken in a conical flask) against dilute hydrochloric acid, which indicator is most suitable and what is the colour change observed at the end point?
questions.solution:
The titration is between ammonium hydroxide ($NH_4OH$), a weak base, and dilute hydrochloric acid ($HCl$), a strong acid.

The salt formed at the equivalence point is ammonium chloride ($NH_4Cl$), which undergoes cationic hydrolysis to give an acidic solution with a pH less than $7$.

For a strong acid-weak base titration, an indicator with a working pH range in the acidic region is required. Methyl orange, which has a pH range of $3.1$ to $4.4$, is the most suitable indicator.

Since the weak base ($NH_4OH$) is taken in the conical flask, the initial medium is basic. Methyl orange is yellow in a basic medium.

As the strong acid ($HCl$) is added from the burette, the pH decreases. At the end point, the solution becomes slightly acidic, and the colour of methyl orange changes to red.

Thus, the observed colour change at the end point is yellow to red.

Answer: Methyl orange, yellow to red

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Aniline (boiling point $184^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$) is often purified from a crude mixture using steam distillation. Which of the following statements correctly describe the principles of this purification process?

I. The aniline-water mixture will boil at a temperature strictly below $100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.
II. At the boiling point of the mixture, the vapor pressure of aniline alone is equal to the atmospheric pressure.
III. Steam distillation is effective because aniline and water are completely miscible liquids.
IV. The mixture boils when the sum of the vapor pressures of water and aniline equals the atmospheric pressure.
questions.solution:
Steam distillation is a separation process used to purify temperature-sensitive organic compounds that are immiscible with water.

In steam distillation, the mixture of immiscible liquids (aniline and water) boils when the sum of their individual vapor pressures equals the atmospheric pressure. This means $P_{\text{total}} = P_{\text{water}} + P_{\text{aniline}} = P_{\text{atm}}$. Therefore, Statement IV is correct, and Statement II is incorrect.

Because the total vapor pressure reaches atmospheric pressure at a lower temperature than the boiling point of either pure component, the mixture will boil at a temperature below the boiling point of pure water ($100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Steam distillation is specifically applicable to liquids that are immiscible with water. Aniline and water are immiscible, not completely miscible. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect.

Thus, only statements I and IV are correct.

Answer: I and IV only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the IUPAC name of the major product $Y$ formed in the following reaction sequence.
questions.solution:
The starting material is 1-methoxy-4-nitrobenzene.

In the first reaction, treatment with $Br_2 / FeBr_3$ results in electrophilic aromatic bromination. The $-OCH_3$ group is strongly activating and ortho/para directing, whereas the $-NO_2$ group is deactivating and meta directing. Both groups synergistically direct the incoming electrophile ($Br^+$) to the position ortho to the $-OCH_3$ group. The product formed is 2-bromo-1-methoxy-4-nitrobenzene.

Next, reaction with $Fe / HCl$ reduces the nitro ($-NO_2$) group to an amino ($-NH_2$) group, yielding 4-amino-2-bromo-1-methoxybenzene.

Subsequent reaction with $NaNO_2 / HCl$ at $273-278$ K (diazotization) converts the primary amine into a diazonium salt, forming 3-bromo-4-methoxybenzenediazonium chloride.

Finally, reaction with $CuCN / KCN$ (Sandmeyer reaction) replaces the diazonium group ($-N_2^+Cl^-$) with a cyano ($-CN$) group.

The final product Y has a $-CN$ group, a $-OCH_3$ group para to it, and a $-Br$ group ortho to the $-OCH_3$ group. According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, the principal functional group is the nitrile ($-CN$), making the parent structure benzonitrile. The carbon atom attached to the $-CN$ group is assigned position 1. Numbering the ring to provide the lowest locants to the substituents places the bromo group at position 3 and the methoxy group at position 4. Therefore, the IUPAC name of product Y is 3-bromo-4-methoxybenzonitrile.

Answer: 3-Bromo-4-methoxybenzonitrile

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the mass of oxalic acid dihydrate needed to prepare $500 \text{ mL}$ of a $0.02 \text{ M}$ aqueous solution.
(Molar mass of $H_2C_2O_4 \cdot 2H_2O = 126 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Molarity of the solution is given by $M = \dfrac{n}{V}$, where $n$ is the number of moles of solute and $V$ is the volume of the solution in liters.

Given $M = 0.02 \text{ M}$ and $V = 500 \text{ mL} = 0.5 \text{ L}$.

Number of moles of oxalic acid dihydrate required is $n = 0.02 \times 0.5 = 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

Molar mass of oxalic acid dihydrate ($H_2C_2O_4 \cdot 2H_2O$) is $126 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

Mass required $= n \times \text{Molar mass} = 0.01 \times 126 = 1.26 \text{ g}$.

Answer: $1.26 \text{ g}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An electrolyte concentration cell consists of two identical metallic electrodes dipped in solutions of the same electrolyte but at different concentrations. Which of the following statements correctly describes the standard cell potential ($E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}$) for such a cell?
options: It is always positive to drive the spontaneous flow of electrons.
It is zero because both half-cells have the same standard reduction potential.
It is determined by the ratio of the electrolyte concentrations in the two half-cells.
It is negative, meaning the cell requires an external voltage to operate.
questions.solution:
For an electrolyte concentration cell, the electrodes and the electrolyte are identical in both half-cells.

The standard cell potential $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}$ is the potential of the cell when all species are at their standard states (unit activity or $1\text{ M}$ concentration).

Since both half-cells are identical under standard conditions, their standard reduction potentials are equal.

$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{\circ}_{\text{anode}} = 0$

The actual cell potential $E_{\text{cell}}$ depends on the concentration ratio according to the Nernst equation, but the standard cell potential is always zero.

Answer: It is zero because both half-cells have the same standard reduction potential.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The initial rate of a chemical reaction, $P + Q \rightarrow \text{Products}$, was measured at various initial concentrations of the reactants. The experimental data is provided in the accompanying table.

Based on this data, which of the following represents the correct rate law for the reaction?
questions.solution:
Let the rate law be $\text{Rate} = k[P]^x[Q]^y$.

From Experiment 1 and 2, when $[Q]$ is kept constant at $0.02 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$, the concentration of $[P]$ is increased from $0.02$ to $0.06$ (by a factor of $3$). The rate increases from $4.0 \times 10^{-5}$ to $1.2 \times 10^{-4}$ (by a factor of $3$).
$\dfrac{\text{Rate}_2}{\text{Rate}_1} = \dfrac{k(0.06)^x(0.02)^y}{k(0.02)^x(0.02)^y}$
$\dfrac{1.2 \times 10^{-4}}{4.0 \times 10^{-5}} = \left(\dfrac{0.06}{0.02}\right)^x$
$3 = 3^x \Rightarrow x = 1$

From Experiment 2 and 3, when $[P]$ is kept constant at $0.06 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$, the concentration of $[Q]$ is increased from $0.02$ to $0.04$ (by a factor of $2$). The rate increases from $1.2 \times 10^{-4}$ to $4.8 \times 10^{-4}$ (by a factor of $4$).
$\dfrac{\text{Rate}_3}{\text{Rate}_2} = \dfrac{k(0.06)^x(0.04)^y}{k(0.06)^x(0.02)^y}$
$\dfrac{4.8 \times 10^{-4}}{1.2 \times 10^{-4}} = \left(\dfrac{0.04}{0.02}\right)^y$
$4 = 2^y \Rightarrow y = 2$

Therefore, the rate law is $\text{Rate} = k[P][Q]^2$.

Answer: $\text{Rate} = k[P][Q]^2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The given figure displays the Arrhenius plots ($\ln k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$) for two distinct chemical reactions, labeled as Reaction X and Reaction Y. Based on the provided graph, identify the correct relationship between their activation energies ($E_a$).
options: $E_a$ of Reaction X < $E_a$ of Reaction Y
$E_a$ of Reaction X > $E_a$ of Reaction Y
$E_a$ of Reaction X = $E_a$ of Reaction Y
Activation energy cannot be compared without knowing the exact temperature range.
questions.solution:
According to the Arrhenius equation:

$k = A e^{-E_a / RT}$

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides, we get:

$\ln k = \ln A - \dfrac{E_a}{R} \left(\dfrac{1}{T}\right)$

This represents a straight line equation $y = mx + c$, where the y-axis is $\ln k$ and the x-axis is $\dfrac{1}{T}$.

The slope of the line is given by $m = -\dfrac{E_a}{R}$.

From the given graph, the line for Reaction X is steeper (more negative) than the line for Reaction Y. This means the magnitude of the slope for Reaction X is greater than that for Reaction Y.

$\left| m_X \right| \gt \left| m_Y \right|$

$\dfrac{E_{a,X}}{R} \gt \dfrac{E_{a,Y}}{R}$

$E_{a,X} \gt E_{a,Y}$

Therefore, the activation energy of Reaction X is greater than the activation energy of Reaction Y.

Answer: $E_a$ of Reaction X > $E_a$ of Reaction Y

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution of potassium dichromate is orange in colour. On adding an alkali to this solution, the colour changes to yellow. This colour change is due to the formation of:
questions.solution:
In aqueous solution, dichromate ions and chromate ions exist in equilibrium depending on the pH of the solution.

$Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 2OH^- \rightleftharpoons 2CrO_4^{2-} + H_2O$

The dichromate ion ($Cr_2O_7^{2-}$) is orange in colour, while the chromate ion ($CrO_4^{2-}$) is yellow. On adding an alkali, the concentration of $OH^-$ increases, shifting the equilibrium to the right and forming yellow $CrO_4^{2-}$ ions.

Answer: $CrO_4^{2-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Unlike transition metal complexes, the colors of lanthanoid(III) complexes are generally not affected by the nature of the ligands. The primary reason for this behavior is that:
options: the $4f$ orbitals are deeply buried and effectively shielded by $5s$ and $5p$ electrons.
the energy difference between $4f$ and $5d$ orbitals is very small, allowing rapid electron exchange.
lanthanoids do not undergo $f-f$ transitions in the presence of strong field ligands.
the $4f$ electrons are strongly repelled by the ligands, preventing any interaction.
questions.solution:
The colors of lanthanoid(III) complexes arise mainly from $f-f$ transitions.

The $4f$ orbitals in lanthanoids are deeply buried inside the atom and are effectively shielded from the external environment by the filled $5s$ and $5p$ orbitals.

Due to this shielding, the $4f$ electrons do not interact significantly with the ligands.

Consequently, the crystal field splitting of the $4f$ orbitals is very small, and the energy levels of the $4f$ orbitals are largely unaffected by the nature of the ligands.

Thus, the colors of lanthanoid(III) complexes remain essentially the same regardless of the ligands present.

Answer: the $4f$ orbitals are deeply buried and effectively shielded by $5s$ and $5p$ electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The oxidation states shown by Mn in the given reaction are :
$2 \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-} + 3 \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 2 \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 5 \mathrm{MnO}_2 + 4 \mathrm{H}^{+}$
A. +6
B. +4
C. +3
D. +7
E. +2
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
In $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}$, let the oxidation state of Mn be $x$.

$x + 4(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow x = +7$

In $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$, the oxidation state of Mn is $+2$.

In $\mathrm{MnO}_2$, let the oxidation state of Mn be $y$.

$y + 2(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow y = +4$

The oxidation states shown by Mn in the given reaction are $+7$, $+2$, and $+4$.

These correspond to D, E, and B respectively.

Answer: B, D and E only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ions or molecules acts as an ambidentate ligand in coordination compounds?
questions.solution:
An ambidentate ligand is a monodentate ligand that contains more than one coordinating atom and can coordinate to the central metal ion through either of them.

The $\text{NO}_2^{-}$ ion has two donor atoms: nitrogen and oxygen. It can bind to the central metal ion either through the nitrogen atom (forming a nitro complex) or through an oxygen atom (forming a nitrito complex).

$\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ (oxalate) and $\text{NH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (ethylenediamine) are bidentate ligands.

$\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is a monodentate ligand with only oxygen as the donor atom.

Thus, $\text{NO}_2^{-}$ acts as an ambidentate ligand.

Answer: $\text{NO}_2^{-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ethylenediaminetetraacetate ($\mathrm{EDTA}^{4-}$) is a widely used ligand in coordination chemistry. Which of the following correctly describes its denticity and the nature of its donor atoms?
options: Hexadentate; two nitrogen and four oxygen donor atoms
Hexadentate; four nitrogen and two oxygen donor atoms
Tetradentate; two nitrogen and two oxygen donor atoms
questions.solution:
Ethylenediaminetetraacetate ($\mathrm{EDTA}^{4-}$) is a hexadentate ligand.

Its chemical structure is $(\mathrm{^-OOC-CH_2})_2\mathrm{N-CH_2-CH_2-N}(\mathrm{CH_2-COO^-})_2$.

It coordinates to a central metal ion through six donor atoms: two nitrogen atoms (each having a lone pair of electrons) and four oxygen atoms (from the four acetate groups).

Answer: Hexadentate; two nitrogen and four oxygen donor atoms

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the major product $\mathrm{R}$ formed in the following reaction sequence:

$\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2COOH} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\mathrm{NH_3}} \mathrm{P} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2/KOH}} \mathrm{Q} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \mathrm{H_2O}]{\text{(i) } \mathrm{NaNO_2 + HCl}} \mathrm{R}$
questions.solution:
Reaction of phenylacetic acid with ammonia followed by heating yields phenylacetamide.

$\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2COOH} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\mathrm{NH_3}} \mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CONH_2}$ (P)

Phenylacetamide undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation on treatment with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ and $\mathrm{KOH}$ to form benzylamine.

$\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CONH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2/KOH}} \mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2NH_2}$ (Q)

Benzylamine, being a primary aliphatic amine, reacts with nitrous acid (generated in situ from $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$ and $\mathrm{HCl}$) to form an unstable diazonium salt. This salt decomposes to give a benzyl carbocation, which is trapped by water to form benzyl alcohol.

$\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2NH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaNO_2 + HCl}} [\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2N_2^+Cl^-}] \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2O}} \mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2OH}$ (R)

Answer: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the major product 'Z' in the following sequence of reactions:

$\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2-CH_2-Br} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{alc. KOH}} \mathrm{X} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HBr}} \mathrm{Y} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{aq. KOH}} \mathrm{Z}$
questions.solution:
The given sequence of reactions proceeds as follows:

$\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2-CH_2-Br}$ undergoes dehydrohalogenation (elimination) in the presence of alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$ and heat to form phenylethene (styrene).
$\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2-CH_2-Br} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{alc. KOH}} \mathrm{C_6H_5-CH=CH_2}$ (X)

Phenylethene undergoes electrophilic addition with $\mathrm{HBr}$. According to Markovnikov's rule, the addition proceeds via the more stable benzylic carbocation intermediate, yielding 1-bromo-1-phenylethane.
$\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH=CH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HBr}} \mathrm{C_6H_5-CH(Br)-CH_3}$ (Y)

1-bromo-1-phenylethane undergoes nucleophilic substitution with aqueous $\mathrm{KOH}$, replacing the bromide ion with a hydroxide ion to form 1-phenylethanol.
$\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH(Br)-CH_3} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{aq. KOH}} \mathrm{C_6H_5-CH(OH)-CH_3}$ (Z)

The major product 'Z' is 1-Phenylethanol.

Answer: 1-Phenylethanol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the chemical reaction scheme shown in the given figure.

Which of the following statements is correct regarding the major products $Y$ and $Z$?
options: Product $Y$ is methanamine and product $Z$ is acetic acid.
Both $Y$ and $Z$ are primary amines, but $Z$ contains one carbon atom less than $X$.
$Y$ and $Z$ are successive members of the same homologous series.
Product $Z$ gives a positive carbylamine test whereas product $Y$ does not.
questions.solution:
Reaction of acetic acid with ammonia followed by heating yields acetamide.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_3, \Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2$ (X)

Acetamide (X) undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation upon reaction with $\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$ to form a primary amine with one carbon atom less, which is methanamine.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2, \text{NaOH}} \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ (Y)

Acetamide (X) undergoes reduction with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ to form a primary amine with the same number of carbon atoms, which is ethanamine.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{(i) LiAlH}_4, \text{ether} \text{ (ii) H}_2\text{O}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (Z)

Y is methanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$) and Z is ethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$).

Both are primary amines and differ by a $-\text{CH}_2-$ unit. Therefore, they are successive members of the same homologous series.

Both Y and Z will give a positive carbylamine test since they are primary amines.

Answer: $Y$ and $Z$ are successive members of the same homologous series.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following amines will produce an intensely foul-smelling substance when heated with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide, but fails to form a stable diazonium salt at $273 - 278\text{ K}$?
questions.solution:
The formation of an intensely foul-smelling substance when heated with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide is the carbylamine reaction, which is a characteristic test for primary amines (both aliphatic and aromatic).

The failure to form a stable diazonium salt at $273 - 278\text{ K}$ indicates that the amine is an aliphatic primary amine. Aromatic primary amines form stable diazonium salts at this temperature due to resonance stabilization, whereas aliphatic primary amines form highly unstable diazonium salts that immediately decompose to yield alcohols and nitrogen gas.

Evaluating the given options:
Benzylamine ($C_6H_5CH_2NH_2$) is a primary aliphatic amine. It gives a positive carbylamine test but fails to form a stable diazonium salt.
$p$-Toluidine and $p$-Chloroaniline are primary aromatic amines. They give a positive carbylamine test and form stable diazonium salts at $273 - 278\text{ K}$.
$N$-Methylaniline is a secondary amine and does not give the carbylamine test.

Therefore, benzylamine is the correct answer.

Answer: Benzylamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The given figure shows the potential energy curves for four hydrogen halide molecules as a function of internuclear distance. Match the curves given in List I with the corresponding molecules in List II.

List IList II
ACurve PI$HBr$
BCurve QII$HF$
CCurve RIII$HI$
DCurve SIV$HCl$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The minimum of a potential energy curve indicates the equilibrium internuclear distance (bond length) on the x-axis and the bond dissociation energy (depth of the potential well) on the y-axis.

As the size of the halogen atom increases down the group ($F \lt Cl \lt Br \lt I$), the bond length of the corresponding hydrogen halide increases: $HF \lt HCl \lt HBr \lt HI$.

Conversely, as bond length increases, bond strength decreases. Thus, the bond dissociation energy follows the order: $HF \gt HCl \gt HBr \gt HI$.

Analyzing the curves:
Curve P has the shortest bond length and highest bond energy, so it represents $HF$ (A \rightarrow II).
Curve Q has the second shortest bond length and second highest bond energy, representing $HCl$ (B \rightarrow IV).
Curve R represents $HBr$ (C \rightarrow I).
Curve S has the longest bond length and lowest bond energy, representing $HI$ (D \rightarrow III).

The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the reaction $2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g})$ at $400\text{ K}$, the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) is $-70\text{ kJ}$. What will be the enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) for the reaction at the same temperature?
(Given $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $2\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NO}_2(\mathrm{g})$

The change in the number of moles of gaseous species is:

$\Delta n_g = n_p - n_r = 2 - (2 + 1) = -1$

The relation between enthalpy change and internal energy change is:

$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H = -70 + (-1) \times (8.314 \times 10^{-3}) \times 400$

$\Delta H = -70 - 3.3256$

$\Delta H = -73.3256\text{ kJ} \approx -73.33\text{ kJ}$

Answer: $-73.33\text{ kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The solubility of $\text{AgSCN}$ in pure water is $x$ times its solubility in a $0.001\text{ M KSCN}$ solution. The value of $x$ is:
(Given : $K_{sp}$ of $\text{AgSCN} = 10^{-12}$)
questions.solution:
Let the solubility of $\text{AgSCN}$ in pure water be $s_1$.

For pure water:
$\text{AgSCN}(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{Ag}^+(aq) + \text{SCN}^-(aq)$
$K_{sp} = s_1^2$
$s_1 = \sqrt{10^{-12}} = 10^{-6}\text{ M}$

Let the solubility of $\text{AgSCN}$ in $0.001\text{ M KSCN}$ be $s_2$.
Due to the common ion effect, $[\text{SCN}^-] = s_2 + 0.001 \approx 10^{-3}\text{ M}$ (since $s_2$ is very small compared to $10^{-3}$).
$K_{sp} = [\text{Ag}^+][\text{SCN}^-] = s_2 \times 10^{-3}$
$s_2 = \dfrac{10^{-12}}{10^{-3}} = 10^{-9}\text{ M}$

Given that $s_1 = x \times s_2$
$x = \dfrac{s_1}{s_2} = \dfrac{10^{-6}}{10^{-9}} = 10^3$

Answer: $10^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During the elemental analysis of a newly synthesized drug molecule, $0.45\text{ g}$ of the sample was subjected to Liebig's combustion method. The experiment yielded $0.66\text{ g}$ of carbon dioxide and $0.27\text{ g}$ of water. What are the respective percentages of carbon and hydrogen in the drug sample?
questions.solution:
Mass of organic compound, $W = 0.45\text{ g}$

Mass of $CO_2$ formed $= 0.66\text{ g}$

Mass of $H_2O$ formed $= 0.27\text{ g}$

Percentage of carbon is given by:

$\% C = \dfrac{12}{44} \times \dfrac{\text{Mass of } CO_2}{\text{Mass of compound}} \times 100$

$\% C = \dfrac{12}{44} \times \dfrac{0.66}{0.45} \times 100 = \dfrac{12}{44} \times \dfrac{66}{45} \times 100 = 40\%$

Percentage of hydrogen is given by:

$\% H = \dfrac{2}{18} \times \dfrac{\text{Mass of } H_2O}{\text{Mass of compound}} \times 100$

$\% H = \dfrac{2}{18} \times \dfrac{0.27}{0.45} \times 100 = \dfrac{1}{9} \times \dfrac{27}{45} \times 100 = 6.67\%$

Answer: $40\%$ and $6.67\%$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The carbon-carbon single bond length in propene ($CH_3-CH=CH_2$) is observed to be slightly shorter than the standard C-C single bond length in propane ($154 \text{ pm}$). Which electronic effect is primarily responsible for imparting this partial double bond character to the single bond in propene?
questions.solution:
In propene ($CH_3-CH=CH_2$), the alkyl group ($CH_3$) is attached to an $sp^2$ hybridized carbon atom of the double bond.

The $\sigma$ electrons of the C-H bonds in the methyl group undergo delocalization with the adjacent $\pi$ electron system of the double bond. This phenomenon is known as hyperconjugation or no-bond resonance.

Due to this hyperconjugative electron delocalization, the carbon-carbon single bond ($C_2-C_3$) acquires a partial double bond character. As a result, the bond length decreases from the standard C-C single bond length of $154 \text{ pm}$ in propane to approximately $150 \text{ pm}$ in propene.

Answer: Hyperconjugation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the skeletal structures of the four hydrocarbons shown below.

Which of these hydrocarbons will be oxidized to the corresponding alcohol upon treatment with potassium permanganate ($\mathrm{KMnO}_4$)?
questions.solution:
Alkanes are generally resistant to oxidation by strong oxidizing agents like $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$.

However, alkanes containing a tertiary hydrogen atom can be oxidized to the corresponding tertiary alcohol by $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$.

Let us analyze the given hydrocarbons:
Compound I (n-pentane) contains only primary ($1^\circ$) and secondary ($2^\circ$) hydrogen atoms.
Compound II (2-methylbutane) contains a tertiary ($3^\circ$) hydrogen atom at the second carbon.
Compound III (2,2-dimethylpropane) contains only primary ($1^\circ$) hydrogen atoms.
Compound IV (cyclohexane) contains only secondary ($2^\circ$) hydrogen atoms.

Since only Compound II has a tertiary hydrogen atom, it will be oxidized to 2-methylbutan-2-ol upon treatment with $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$.

Answer: Compound II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A solution is prepared by dissolving $W$ grams of a non-electrolyte polymer (molar mass $= 6000 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$) in enough water to make $500 \text{ mL}$ of solution. This solution is found to be isotonic with a solution containing $0.18 \text{ g}$ of glucose ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O}_6$) per $100 \text{ mL}$ at the same temperature. The value of $W$ is:

(Given atomic masses in $\mathrm{g~mol}^{-1}$: $\mathrm{C}: 12, \mathrm{H}: 1, \mathrm{O}: 16$)
questions.solution:
For isotonic solutions at the same temperature, their osmotic pressures are equal. Since both the polymer and glucose are non-electrolytes, their van 't Hoff factors are $i=1$, which implies their molar concentrations must be equal.

Molar mass of glucose ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O}_6$) $= 6 \times 12 + 12 \times 1 + 6 \times 16 = 180 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Concentration of glucose solution, $C_2 = \dfrac{0.18}{180} \times \dfrac{1000}{100} = 0.01 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

Concentration of polymer solution, $C_1 = \dfrac{W}{6000} \times \dfrac{1000}{500} = \dfrac{W}{3000} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

Equating the concentrations $C_1 = C_2$:

$\dfrac{W}{3000} = 0.01$

$W = 30 \text{ g}$

Answer: $30 \text{ g}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the galvanic cell reaction given below:
$2\mathrm{Cr(s)} + 3\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}\mathrm{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}\mathrm{(aq)} + 3\mathrm{Cd(s)}$

The standard cell potential ($E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}$) is $0.34\text{ V}$. Calculate the standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^{\circ}$) for the reaction.
(Given: $1\text{ F} = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The given cell reaction is:

$2\mathrm{Cr(s)} + 3\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}\mathrm{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}\mathrm{(aq)} + 3\mathrm{Cd(s)}$

The number of electrons transferred in the balanced reaction is $n = 6$.

The standard Gibbs free energy change is given by the relation:

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -6 \times 96500 \times 0.34$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -196860\text{ J mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -196.86\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-196.86\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For a first-order decomposition reaction, the half-life period decreases from $40 \text{ minutes}$ at $27^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $20 \text{ minutes}$ at $37^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. What is the activation energy of this reaction?
(Given: $\log 2 = 0.301, \mathrm{R} = 8.314 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, the rate constant is inversely proportional to the half-life: $k = \dfrac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}$.

At $T_1 = 27^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 300 \text{ K}$, $t_{1/2} = 40 \text{ min}$, so $k_1 = \dfrac{0.693}{40}$.

At $T_2 = 37^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 310 \text{ K}$, $t_{1/2} = 20 \text{ min}$, so $k_2 = \dfrac{0.693}{20}$.

Taking the ratio of the rate constants:

$\dfrac{k_2}{k_1} = \dfrac{40}{20} = 2$

Using the Arrhenius equation:

$\log \left( \dfrac{k_2}{k_1} \right) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left( \dfrac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2} \right)$

Substituting the given values:

$\log 2 = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 \times 8.314} \left( \dfrac{310 - 300}{300 \times 310} \right)$

$0.301 = \dfrac{E_a}{19.147} \left( \dfrac{10}{93000} \right)$

$E_a = \dfrac{0.301 \times 19.147 \times 93000}{10}$

$E_a = 53598 \text{ J mol}^{-1} = 53.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $53.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The given reaction illustrates the direct iodination of ethylbenzene. Unlike chlorination or bromination, this reaction is reversible due to the formation of a strong reducing byproduct. To drive the equilibrium in the forward direction, Reagent Z is required. Identify the most suitable Reagent Z from the following.
questions.solution:
Direct iodination of aromatic compounds is a reversible process because the byproduct, $HI$, is a strong reducing agent. It reduces the formed iodoarene back to the starting arene.

$Ar-H + I_2 \rightleftharpoons Ar-I + HI$

To drive the equilibrium in the forward direction, the $HI$ produced must be consumed. This is achieved by carrying out the reaction in the presence of an oxidizing agent such as $HIO_3$, $HIO_4$, or $HNO_3$.

The oxidizing agent oxidizes $HI$ to $I_2$, thereby preventing the reverse reaction and shifting the equilibrium to the right:

$7HI + HIO_4 \rightarrow 4I_2 + 4H_2O$

Among the given options, $HIO_4$ is the only suitable oxidizing agent.

Answer: $HIO_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I (Reagent/Test) with List II (Ion identified) based on the characteristic precipitates or colors formed in qualitative analysis:

List IList II
ADimethylglyoximeI$Pb^{2+}$
BPotassium chromateII$Cu^{2+}$
CSodium nitroprussideIII$Ni^{2+}$
DPotassium ferrocyanideIV$S^{2-}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Dimethylglyoxime reacts with $Ni^{2+}$ in an ammoniacal medium to form a rosy red precipitate of $Ni(DMG)_2$. This corresponds to test tube A. Thus, A \rightarrow III.

Potassium chromate reacts with $Pb^{2+}$ to form a yellow precipitate of lead chromate, $PbCrO_4$. This corresponds to test tube B. Thus, B \rightarrow I.

Sodium nitroprusside reacts with sulfide ions ($S^{2-}$) to form a purple-violet complex, $[Fe(CN)_5NOS]^{4-}$. This corresponds to test tube C. Thus, C \rightarrow IV.

Potassium ferrocyanide reacts with $Cu^{2+}$ to form a chocolate brown precipitate of copper ferrocyanide, $Cu_2[Fe(CN)_6]$. This corresponds to test tube D. Thus, D \rightarrow II.

The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
During the qualitative analysis of salts using dilute acids, various gases are evolved which are identified by their specific confirmatory tests. Match the gases evolved in List I with their characteristic confirmatory tests in List II.

List I (Gas Evolved)List II (Characteristic Test)
A$CO_2$1Turns acidified $K_2Cr_2O_7$ paper green
B$H_2S$2Turns lead acetate paper black
C$SO_2$3Turns starch-iodide paper blue
D$NO_2$4Turns lime water milky

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
A. $CO_2$ gas turns lime water milky due to the formation of insoluble calcium carbonate ($CaCO_3$).
$Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2 \rightarrow CaCO_3 \downarrow + H_2O$
Thus, A matches with 4.

B. $H_2S$ gas turns lead acetate paper black due to the formation of black lead sulfide ($PbS$).
$(CH_3COO)_2Pb + H_2S \rightarrow PbS \downarrow + 2CH_3COOH$
Thus, B matches with 2.

C. $SO_2$ gas turns acidified potassium dichromate ($K_2Cr_2O_7$) paper green because it reduces $Cr^{6+}$ (orange) to $Cr^{3+}$ (green).
$K_2Cr_2O_7 + 3SO_2 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow K_2SO_4 + Cr_2(SO_4)_3 + H_2O$
Thus, C matches with 1.

D. $NO_2$ gas acts as an oxidizing agent and oxidizes iodide ions to iodine, which turns starch-iodide paper blue.
$2NO_2 + 2KI \rightarrow 2KNO_2 + I_2$
$I_2 + \text{starch} \rightarrow \text{blue complex}$
Thus, D matches with 3.

The correct matching is A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3.

Answer: A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Pteridophytes are further classified into four classes. Which of the given plants is correctly paired with the class it belongs to?
questions.solution:
Pteridophytes are classified into four classes:

Psilopsida: Psilotum

Lycopsida: Selaginella, Lycopodium
